title: One-Hand Push-Dribble Coordination
description: Players dribble the ball with one hand while the other hand works the push rim, the exact coordination needed to advance the ball and the chair together.

content.objective: Dribble with one hand while the other pushes the chair forward, without losing rhythm in either.
content.setup: Players start at half court with a ball and open space ahead.
instructions: Dribble with the right hand while pushing the right wheel with short strokes of the same hand, alternating with left-hand pushes to keep the chair straight.
Push a few strokes, dribble a few touches, finding a rhythm that keeps both going.
Push the length of the court maintaining the dribble the whole way.
Switch dribbling hands halfway and repeat back the other way.
coachingPoints: Accept a slower pace at first — rhythm matters more than speed early on.
Keep the dribble low so it doesn't interfere with the push stroke.
Use the off-hand for extra push strokes when the dribbling hand is busy.
commonMistakes: Stopping the dribble completely every time a push stroke is needed.
Losing the straight line because only one side is pushing.
Letting the off-hand drop instead of staying ready to protect the ball.
content.safety: Make sure the full-court lane is clear before pushing at speed.
